sounds.name: Warm Pad
sounds.ref: In the style of 1980s film-score synth pads
sounds.blurb: A slow, warm chord wash that swells in and hangs in the air.
sounds.how: Two sawtooth oscillators a few cents apart beat against each other, which is what makes a polysynth pad sound alive. Slow attacks on both envelopes fade each chord in, and Envelope 1 opens the filter as it swells. VINTAGE lets the five voices drift apart and the reverb puts the chords in a room.

steps.title: Two sawtooths, a few cents apart
steps.why:
A pad starts with two oscillators that are nearly, but not quite, in tune.
- OSC 2 at 60 % and OSC 1 at 60 %: both sawtooths (SHAPE at the middle), equally loud.
- OSC 2 PITCH +0.1 st: a few cents sharp. The two waves drift in and out of step, so each note slowly swirls.
- Listen for: a gentle, slow beating inside every note. Back to 0 and it goes flat and still.

steps.title: Fade each chord in and out
steps.why:
Envelope 2 runs the volume (ENV ROUTING is on its first setting, so Envelope 2 is Amp).
- Envelope 2 ATTACK 1.1 s: each chord fades in rather than starting at once.
- RELEASE 1.6 s: the chord lingers after you let go, so one chord melts into the next.
- Listen for: soft beginnings and long tails. SUSTAIN stays at full, so held chords do not fade.

steps.title: Let the filter swell open
steps.why:
Envelope 1 runs the filter. Starting dark and opening slowly makes the pad bloom.
- CUTOFF 216 Hz: dark at rest.
- Envelope 1 AMOUNT +2.0, ATTACK 1.6 s, DECAY 1.6 s, SUSTAIN 40 %, RELEASE 1.6 s: the filter opens over about two seconds, then settles part way back.
- Listen for: each chord getting brighter as it swells, then mellowing.

steps.title: Age it and give it a room
steps.why:
The last touches make it sound like an old instrument in a real space.
- VINTAGE 40 %: each voice wanders slightly out of tune on its own, like the voices of an old polysynth.
- REVERB on, MIX 40 %, DECAY 70 %: a long, soft tail.
- Listen for: the chord sounding wider and further away.

context.osc2.pitch: The detune. A few cents gives the slow swirl; more turns it sour.
context.env2.attack: How slowly each chord fades in.
context.env1.attack: How slowly the filter opens: the bloom.
context.voice.vintage: How far the five voices drift from each other.

tweaks.hear: A faster, seasick chorus in every note.
The swell turns into a bright, brassy bloom.

sounds.name: Poly Brass
sounds.ref: In the style of Van Halen — "Jump"
sounds.blurb: Bright, punchy synth-brass chords with a quick swell at the front of each stab.
sounds.how: Synth brass is two sawtooths through a filter that an envelope opens fast and closes part way: the bright "blare" at the front of each note is the filter, not the volume. A short attack on the filter envelope gives the slight swell a brass player makes. The stabs are short, so the decay shape is what you hear.

steps.title: Two bright sawtooths
steps.why:
Brass needs a bright, buzzy start.
- OSC 2 60 %, OSC 1 60 %: both sawtooths, which are full of the harmonics brass has.
- OSC 2 PITCH -0.1 st: a touch flat of Oscillator 1, for thickness.
- Listen for: a full, raw buzz.

steps.title: Make the filter blare
steps.why:
The brass "blare" is the filter opening fast at the start of each note and settling back.
- CUTOFF 154 Hz: fairly dark between notes.
- Envelope 1 AMOUNT +3.0: a big sweep upward.
- ATTACK 48 ms: not instant, so each stab swells in like a breath.
- DECAY 460 ms, SUSTAIN 30 %: it falls back to a mellower held tone.
- Listen for: "bwaah" on every stab.

steps.title: Shape the volume
steps.why:
Envelope 2 shapes the loudness.
- ATTACK 8 ms: a tiny fade-in, so the stabs do not click.
- RELEASE 75 ms: a short tail after each stab.
- Listen for: tight, punchy chords.

steps.title: A little room
steps.why:
A short reverb takes the dryness off.
- REVERB on, MIX 20 %, DECAY 30 %.
- Listen for: the stabs ringing slightly into the gaps.

context.env1.amount: How far the filter blares open on each stab.
context.env1.attack: The swell at the front of each note.
context.vcf.cutoff: How dark the sound is between stabs.

tweaks.hear: A harder, more percussive stab with no swell.
Softer notes from a MIDI keyboard blare less.

sounds.name: Sync Sweep Lead
sounds.ref: In the style of early 1980s new-wave sync leads
sounds.blurb: A tearing lead whose tone sweeps down at the start of every note.
sounds.how: SYNC 2→1 makes Oscillator 1 restart with every cycle of Oscillator 2, so Oscillator 2 holds the note and Oscillator 1’s pitch changes only the tone. ENV ROUTING frees Envelope 1 to sweep Oscillator 1’s pitch, so each note starts with a tearing "neow". Envelope 2 then runs both the filter and the volume.

steps.title: Oscillator 1 alone, synced to Oscillator 2
steps.why:
Hard sync is the core of this lead.
- SYNC 2→1 on: Oscillator 1 restarts its wave every time Oscillator 2 starts a cycle. Oscillator 2 now sets the note, even though OSC 2 is down at 0 in the mixer.
- Listen for: no change yet. Both oscillators are at the same pitch, so sync has nothing to tear. Turn OSC 1 PITCH up and the tone turns hard and nasal while the note stays put.

steps.title: Free Envelope 1 to sweep Oscillator 1
steps.why:
ENV ROUTING decides what the envelopes do. Its second setting gives the filter and the volume to Envelope 2, and frees Envelope 1 for a destination of its own (Aux).
- ENV ROUTING: Env 1 Aux / Env 2 Filter+Amp.
- ENV 1 DEST (on the display): Osc 1 Freq.
- Envelope 1 AMOUNT +5.0: at the peak it throws Oscillator 1 an octave above Oscillator 2.
- ATTACK 0, DECAY 460 ms, SUSTAIN 0: the sweep falls away in under half a second.
- Listen for: a tearing "neow" at the front of each note.

steps.title: Set the filter and the volume
steps.why:
Envelope 2 now moves the filter and the volume together, by the same AMOUNT.
- CUTOFF 304 Hz: with Envelope 2 at full AMOUNT and SUSTAIN, the filter opens wide while a key is held.
- Envelope 2 RELEASE 48 ms: a short tail.
- Listen for: the sweep coming through bright, with a quick close when you let go.

steps.title: Glide and echo
steps.why:
Two finishing touches for a lead.
- GLIDE on, GLIDE 90 ms: each note slides briefly into the next.
- EFFECT on, TYPE Stereo delay, TIME 50 %, DEPTH/MIX 25 %, FBACK/MISC 30 %: a few echoes behind the line.
- Listen for: a lead that sings and trails off.

context.osc1.sync: Locks Oscillator 1 to Oscillator 2: the source of the tear.
context.env.routing: The second setting frees Envelope 1 to sweep the pitch.
context.env1.amount: How far the sweep throws Oscillator 1: the size of the tear.
context.env1.decay: How long the sweep takes to fall.

tweaks.hear: A slow, vocal "yeow" on every note.
A harder, more nasal held tone under the sweep.
The held tone jumps to a brighter overtone.

sounds.name: Sub Bass
sounds.ref: In the style of 2010s synthwave basslines
sounds.blurb: A round, heavy bass with a soft pluck at the front of each note.
sounds.how: A square wave from Oscillator 1 with the sub-oscillator an octave below it gives weight without buzz. A dark filter and a short filter envelope add a soft pluck, and the volume envelope lets each note ring briefly.

steps.title: A square with a sub underneath
steps.why:
Weight comes from the sub-oscillator.
- OSC 1 SHAPE square: a square, hollow and round.
- OSC 1 SUB 60 %: a square an octave lower, from Oscillator 1.
- Listen for: a deep, solid low end.

steps.title: Darken it and add a pluck
steps.why:
A dark filter keeps the bass round; a short envelope puts a soft pluck on it.
- CUTOFF 154 Hz.
- Envelope 1 AMOUNT +2.0, DECAY 75 ms, SUSTAIN 0: a quick flick open on each note.
- Listen for: a soft "dum" at the start of every note.

steps.title: Tighten the volume
steps.why:
Envelope 2 shapes each note.
- DECAY 460 ms, SUSTAIN 60 %: each note dips slightly after it starts.
- RELEASE 15 ms: notes stop cleanly.
- Listen for: tight, even notes.

context.vcf.cutoff: How round or buzzy the bass is.
context.env1.amount: The pluck at the front of each note.

tweaks.hear: The filter saturates: thicker and grittier.
How much the weight came from the sub.

sounds.name: FM Bells
sounds.ref: In the style of 1980s digital bell sounds
sounds.blurb: Glassy, metallic bells that ring out and fade.
sounds.how: FM 2→1 lets Oscillator 2 wobble Oscillator 1’s frequency at audio speed, which adds new, inharmonic tones: the clang of a bell. Both oscillators are sine waves, so every overtone comes from the FM. Oscillator 2 is tuned an octave and a fifth up, and the OSC 2 knob sets how hard it modulates.

steps.title: Two sine waves
steps.why:
FM is easiest to hear starting from plain sines.
- OSC 1 SHAPE and OSC 2 SHAPE sine: pure sines, with no overtones of their own.
- OSC 2 OCTAVE +1, PITCH +7 st: an octave and a fifth above Oscillator 1, three times its frequency.
- Listen for: a plain, flute-like tone (Oscillator 2 is still down at 0).

steps.title: Turn on FM
steps.why:
With FM 2→1 on, the OSC 2 knob no longer mixes Oscillator 2 in: it sets how hard Oscillator 2 modulates Oscillator 1.
- FM 2→1 on.
- OSC 2 40 %: enough for a metallic ring without turning harsh.
- CUTOFF 9.1 kHz: the filter stays open so the new overtones come through.
- Listen for: the flute turning into glass and metal.

steps.title: Make it ring and fade
steps.why:
A bell is struck, then rings away.
- Envelope 2 DECAY 1.6 s, SUSTAIN 0, RELEASE 1.6 s: each note fades out over a couple of seconds whether you hold it or not.
- Listen for: struck notes that ring.

steps.title: Put it in a hall
steps.why:
Bells ring in big spaces.
- REVERB on, MIX 40 %, DECAY 70 %, PREDELAY 40 ms.
- Listen for: the notes blooming into a shimmering tail.

context.osc.fm: Turns Oscillator 2 into a modulator of Oscillator 1.
context.mix.osc2: With FM on, how hard Oscillator 2 modulates: the amount of clang.
context.osc2.pitch: The ratio between the two oscillators, which decides which overtones appear.

sounds.name: Unison Lead
sounds.ref: In the style of 1980s synth-rock solos
sounds.blurb: A huge, slightly growling mono lead with vibrato and glide.
sounds.how: UNISON stacks all five voices on one note, slightly detuned, so the lead is ten oscillators thick. Glide slides between notes, LFO 1 adds vibrato, and OVERDRIVE roughens the summed voices.

steps.title: Stack the voices
steps.why:
UNISON plays every voice on the one note.
- UNISON on: all five voices, each slightly detuned.
- OSC 2 60 %, PITCH +0.1 st: Oscillator 2 joins in, a touch sharp.
- Listen for: one note, but massive and moving.

steps.title: Shape the tone
steps.why:
A little resonance and a short filter envelope give the lead a vocal edge.
- CUTOFF 843 Hz, RESONANCE 30 %.
- Envelope 1 AMOUNT +1.5, DECAY 460 ms, SUSTAIN 40 %.
- Listen for: a bright start to each note that settles to a singing tone.

steps.title: Glide and vibrato
steps.why:
The expression of a lead.
- GLIDE on, GLIDE 160 ms: notes slide into each other.
- LFO 1 (the LFO button on 1) FREQUENCY 2.23 Hz, AMOUNT +1.0, DEST Osc All Freq: a gentle vibrato on both oscillators.
- Listen for: a lead that slides and wavers like a voice.

steps.title: Rough it up
steps.why:
OVERDRIVE drives the summed voices before the effects.
- OVERDRIVE 30 %: a light growl.
- EFFECT on, TYPE BBD delay, TIME 50 %, DEPTH/MIX 20 %: a dark echo behind the line.
- Listen for: grit and space.

context.voice.unison: Stacks all five voices on one note.
context.glide.time: How long each note takes to slide to the next.
context.drive.amount: How much the stacked voices growl.

sounds.name: Echoing Arpeggio
sounds.ref: In the style of 1980s synth-pop arpeggios
sounds.blurb: A bright, plucky arpeggio that climbs two octaves and echoes off the beat.
sounds.how: Hold a chord and the arpeggiator plays its notes one at a time, up and down over two octaves, in sixteenths at the BPM. A short, resonant filter pluck gives each note a click, and the BBD delay, set to a dotted eighth, throws the notes back off the beat.

steps.title: Turn the arpeggiator on
steps.why:
The riff holds chords; the arpeggiator breaks them into single notes.
- ARPEGGIATOR ON.
- MODE Up+Down, OCTAVE 2 octaves: up and back down, over two octaves.
- CLK DIV 1/16, BPM 110 BPM: one note per sixteenth.
- Listen for: a running pattern instead of chords.

steps.title: A plucked, resonant tone
steps.why:
Each note gets a quick, resonant flick of the filter.
- CUTOFF 427 Hz, RESONANCE 40 %.
- Envelope 1 AMOUNT +3.0, DECAY 75 ms, SUSTAIN 0.
- Envelope 2 DECAY 190 ms, SUSTAIN 0, RELEASE 48 ms: every note dies away on its own.
- Listen for: a crisp "pew" on every step.

steps.title: Echo it off the beat
steps.why:
The BBD delay is dark and warm, like the bucket-brigade chips of 1980s delays.
- EFFECT on, TYPE BBD delay.
- TIME 82 %: about a dotted eighth (410 ms) at this tempo, so the echoes fall between the notes.
- DEPTH/MIX 35 %, FBACK/MISC 45 %: several echoes, a little under the dry sound.
- Listen for: the pattern answering itself.

context.arp.on: Turns held chords into a running pattern.
context.fx.time: The echo time: set it against the tempo.

tweaks.hear: The same notes in a new order every time.

sounds.name: Velocity Pluck
sounds.ref: In the style of modern synth-pop plucks
sounds.blurb: A short, hollow pluck that brightens the harder you play.
sounds.how: SHAPE between sawtooth and square gives a hollow, woody tone. Envelope 1 snaps the filter open and shut on every note, and VELOCITY makes how far it opens follow how hard each note is played: the riff’s accented notes come out brighter.

steps.title: A hollow wave
steps.why:
Between sawtooth and square, SHAPE gives a tone that is bright but hollow.
- OSC 1 SHAPE saw → square, OSC 1 90 %: up loud, since each pluck is short.
- Listen for: a woody, slightly nasal buzz.

steps.title: Snap the filter
steps.why:
A pluck is a filter that opens at once and closes fast.
- CUTOFF 600 Hz: muted at rest.
- Envelope 1 AMOUNT +4.0, ATTACK 0, DECAY 75 ms, SUSTAIN 0, RELEASE 75 ms.
- Listen for: a quick "plink" on each note.

steps.title: Follow the touch
steps.why:
VELOCITY makes an envelope follow how hard each key is played.
- Envelope 1 VELOCITY on: harder notes open the filter further.
- Envelope 2 DECAY 700 ms, SUSTAIN 0, RELEASE 120 ms: each note dies away like a plucked string.
- Listen for: the riff’s accented notes coming out brighter than the rest.

steps.title: Room around it
steps.why:
- REVERB on, MIX 30 %, DECAY 50 %, TONE thinner 40 %: a medium room with its bass cut so the plucks stay clear.
- Listen for: the notes ringing into a soft tail.

context.env1.vel: Makes the pluck brighter on harder notes.
context.env1.decay: How long the pluck takes to close.
context.osc1.shape: The hollow tone of the pluck.

sounds.name: Rotary Organ
sounds.ref: In the style of 1960s and 70s rock organ
sounds.blurb: A drawbar-style organ through a spinning rotary speaker.
sounds.how: Sine waves at the note, an octave up and an octave down stand in for an organ’s drawbars. The third ENV ROUTING setting gates the volume, so notes switch on and off like an organ’s keys, and the rotating speaker effect swirls the sound.

steps.title: Sine "drawbars"
steps.why:
An organ adds sine waves at different octaves.
- OSC 1 SHAPE sine, OSC 1 35 %: the note itself.
- OSC 2 SHAPE sine, OCTAVE +1, OSC 2 25 %: an octave above.
- OSC 1 SUB 25 %: an octave below.
- CUTOFF 6.5 kHz: the filter stays out of the way.
- Listen for: a pure, round organ tone.

steps.title: Gate the volume
steps.why:
An organ note is on while the key is down and off when it comes up.
- ENV ROUTING: Env 1 Aux / Env 2 Filter+Gate. The volume now simply opens with the key; Envelope 2 still moves the filter.
- Envelope 2 AMOUNT 0: the filter stays where CUTOFF puts it.
- Listen for: instant on, instant off.

steps.title: Spin the speaker
steps.why:
A rotating speaker throws the sound around the room.
- EFFECT on, TYPE Rotating speaker.
- TIME 30 %: the slow speed; above the middle it switches to fast.
- DEPTH/MIX 100 %, FBACK/MISC 40 %: all through the speaker, at a middling distance.
- OVERDRIVE 20 %: a little bite, like a driven organ amplifier.
- Listen for: a slow swirl.

context.env.routing: The gated setting makes the volume switch on and off like an organ.
context.fx.time: The rotor speed: slow below the middle, fast above.

tweaks.hear: The rotors speed up into a fast warble.

sounds.name: Wind
sounds.ref: In the style of 1970s synthesizer sound effects
sounds.blurb: A howling wind made from filtered noise, gusting slowly.
sounds.how: Pink noise through a resonant filter whistles at the cutoff, like air across an opening. LFO 1 sweeps the cutoff slowly up and down for the gusts, and slow envelopes and a long reverb blow it in and out. The oscillators are off: it is all noise.

steps.title: Noise instead of the oscillators
steps.why:
Wind is noise, not a pitch.
- OSC 1 0 %: the oscillators are silent.
- NOISE pink 70 %: pink noise, darker and softer than white.
- Listen for: a steady hiss.

steps.title: Make it whistle
steps.why:
Resonance turns the filter into a whistle at the cutoff.
- CUTOFF 843 Hz, RESONANCE 80 %.
- Listen for: a hollow, howling tone inside the hiss.

steps.title: Gusts from LFO 1
steps.why:
A slow LFO on the cutoff moves the whistle up and down.
- LFO 1 DEST Cutoff, FREQUENCY 0.28 Hz, AMOUNT +2.5, SHAPE triangle.
- Listen for: the howl rising and falling every few seconds.

steps.title: Blow in and out
steps.why:
Slow envelopes and a long reverb make it rise and die away.
- Envelope 2 ATTACK 1.6 s, RELEASE 2.5 s.
- REVERB on, MIX 50 %, DECAY 80 %.
- Listen for: wind that builds, gusts and fades into the distance.

context.mix.noise: The source of the wind: pink to the left, white to the right.

tweaks.hear: The howl jumps between random pitches.
A softer rush with no whistle.

sounds.name: Night Drum Pad
sounds.ref: In the style of Phil Collins — “In the Air Tonight”
sounds.blurb: A dark, hollow, brooding pad that hangs behind a sparse song.
sounds.how: Collins’s pad came from a Prophet-5: two detuned waves through a closed filter, slow in and slow out. Here the square end of SHAPE gives the hollowness, the filter stays dark, and a slow phaser turns it.

steps.title: Two hollow waves
steps.why:
Square waves are hollow: they have only odd harmonics.
- OSC 1 SHAPE square
- OSC 2 SHAPE square, PITCH +0.2 st
- OSC 1 level 50 %, OSC 2 50 %: both equal, Oscillator 2 a few cents sharp
- Listen for: a woody, slowly beating tone.

steps.title: Dark and slow
steps.why:
Keep the filter low and let the chord fade in.
- CUTOFF 216 Hz
- Envelope 2 ATTACK 1.1 s, RELEASE 1.6 s: each chord fades in and lingers
- Listen for: a muffled, brooding swell.

steps.title: Turn it slowly
steps.why:
A slow phaser sweeps a notch through the chord.
- EFFECT on, TYPE Phaser, TIME 20 %, DEPTH/MIX 60 %, FBACK/MISC 40 %: a slow, deep sweep
- REVERB on, MIX 40 %, DECAY 60 %
- Listen for: the pad turning in a dark room.

sounds.name: Sweet Dreams Riff
sounds.ref: In the style of Eurythmics — “Sweet Dreams (Are Made of This)”
sounds.blurb: A cold, rubbery, repeating bass riff with a resonant edge.
sounds.how: The riff is a sawtooth through a resonant filter with a short envelope, so each note has a rubbery “bow”. The sub-oscillator underneath keeps it heavy.

steps.title: Saw and sub
steps.why:
A bright saw with weight underneath.
- OSC 1 level 80 %, OSC 1 SUB 40 %
- Listen for: a full, buzzy bass.

steps.title: A rubbery filter
steps.why:
Resonance and a short envelope give each note its bow.
- CUTOFF 216 Hz, RESONANCE 50 %
- Envelope 1 AMOUNT +3.0, DECAY 120 ms, SUSTAIN 10 %: a quick flick open on each note
- Listen for: a resonant “bow” on every note.

steps.title: Tight notes
steps.why:
- Envelope 2 DECAY 300 ms, SUSTAIN 70 %, RELEASE 30 ms: notes stop cleanly
- Listen for: an even, mechanical riff.

sounds.name: Can’t Get Enough Pluck
sounds.ref: In the style of Depeche Mode — “Just Can’t Get Enough”
sounds.blurb: A bright, bouncy pluck playing a cheerful riff.

steps.why:
- OSC 1 SHAPE pulse 32 %: bright and nasal
- Listen for: a reedy buzz.

steps.title: Pluck it

The filter opens and shuts on every note.

steps.title: A short echo
steps.why:

- OSC 2 PITCH +0.1 st

steps.title: The blare

sounds.name: Tainted Bink
sounds.ref: In the style of Soft Cell — “Tainted Love”
sounds.blurb: A short, pitched “bink-bink” that drops in pitch on every hit.

steps.title: A pure tone
steps.why:
- OSC 1 SHAPE sine → saw: round, with a little edge
- OSC 1 level 100 %: up full, since each hit is short

steps.title: Drop the pitch

ENV ROUTING frees Envelope 1 for pitch.

- ENV 1 DEST Osc All Freq: both oscillators
- Envelope 1 AMOUNT −4.0, DECAY 75 ms, SUSTAIN 0 %: a fast drop into each note
- Listen for: a pitched “bink”.

steps.title: Short and wet
steps.why:

- REVERB on, MIX 50 %, DECAY 60 %
- Listen for: a ringing, dropping hit.

sounds.ref: In the style of Yazoo — “Only You”
sounds.blurb: A sweet, gentle chime playing a tender tune.

steps.title: Mostly sine

- OSC 1 SHAPE sine → saw: a sine with a hint of overtones
- Listen for: a soft, round tone.

sounds.ref: In the style of Simple Minds — “Don’t You (Forget About Me)”

steps.why:

- OSC 2 OCTAVE +1 oct, PITCH +0.1 st
- Listen for: a bright, open chord.

steps.title: A lift on each chord
steps.why:
- CUTOFF 427 Hz
- Envelope 1 AMOUNT +2.0, ATTACK 300 ms, DECAY 1.1 s, SUSTAIN 50 %
- Envelope 2 ATTACK 120 ms, RELEASE 700 ms
- Listen for: each chord opening as it starts.

steps.title: Wide
steps.why:
- EFFECT on, TYPE Chorus, TIME 40 %, DEPTH/MIX 60 %, FBACK/MISC 70 %

- Listen for: a big, wide chorus pad.

sounds.name: Take On Me Lead
sounds.ref: In the style of a-ha — “Take On Me”
sounds.blurb: A bright, bouncy, chirpy lead for a fast riff.
sounds.how: The riff’s lead is a bright square-ish tone with a quick filter flick on each note, up an octave so it cuts through. Short notes keep it bouncing.

steps.title: A bright square
steps.why:

sounds.blurb: An eerie, wailing, wide-vibrato theremin line.
sounds.how: A theremin is a pure tone that slides everywhere with a wide, wobbling vibrato. A sine, long glide and a deep vibrato.

steps.title: A sine
steps.why:
- OSC 1 SHAPE sine → saw, OCTAVE +1 oct
- OSC 1 level 80 %
- CUTOFF 2.3 kHz
- Listen for: a pure tone.

steps.title: Slide
steps.why:
- GLIDE on, time 810 ms
- Envelope 2 ATTACK 48 ms, RELEASE 300 ms
- Listen for: notes sliding.

steps.title: Wail
steps.why:
- LFO 1 DEST Osc All Freq, FREQUENCY 2.75 Hz, AMOUNT +1.1
- REVERB on, MIX 40 %, DECAY 60 %
- Listen for: an eerie theremin.

sounds.name: Buzzy Sub Bass
sounds.ref: In the style of Billie Eilish — “bad guy”
sounds.blurb: A deep, buzzing, distorted sub bass.
sounds.how: A sub bass pushed into OVERDRIVE until it buzzes: the harmonics let it be heard on phone speakers.

steps.title: A sine
steps.why:
- OSC 1 SHAPE sine
- OSC 1 level 100 %, OSC 1 SUB 40 %
- CUTOFF 304 Hz
- Listen for: a deep sub.

steps.title: Buzz
steps.why:
- OVERDRIVE 70 %: a buzzing edge
- Envelope 2 DECAY 460 ms, SUSTAIN 60 %, RELEASE 48 ms
- Listen for: a buzzing sub.

sounds.name: Bouncy Square Bass
sounds.ref: In the style of Grimes — “Oblivion”
sounds.blurb: A bouncy, round, plucky square bass.
sounds.how: A square bass with a short pluck and a little echo: bouncy and light.

steps.title: Square
steps.why:
- OSC 1 SHAPE square
- OSC 1 level 90 %
- CUTOFF 304 Hz
- Envelope 1 AMOUNT +2.5, DECAY 190 ms, SUSTAIN 10 %
- Envelope 2 DECAY 300 ms, SUSTAIN 30 %, RELEASE 48 ms
- Listen for: a bouncy bass.

steps.title: Echo
steps.why:
- EFFECT on, TYPE Stereo delay, TIME 40 %, DEPTH/MIX 15 %, FBACK/MISC 20 %
- Listen for: a light, bouncy bass.

sounds.name: Hyperpop Metal Bass
sounds.ref: In the style of SOPHIE — “Vroom Vroom”
sounds.blurb: A hard, metallic, rubbery bass that sounds like bending plastic.
sounds.how: SOPHIE’s sounds are synthetic and plastic. Hard FM and Envelope 1 sweeping Oscillator 2’s pitch make the timbre bend on every note; OVERDRIVE hardens it.

steps.title: Hard FM
steps.why:
- OSC 1 SHAPE sine
- OSC 2 SHAPE sine
- FM 2→1 on
- OSC 1 level 100 %, OSC 2 60 %
- Listen for: a metallic bass.

steps.title: Bend the metal
steps.why:
- ENV ROUTING Env 1 Aux / Env 2 Filter+Amp: Envelope 2 now runs the filter and the volume; Envelope 1 is free
- ENV 1 DEST Osc 2 Freq: the modulator
- Envelope 1 AMOUNT +4.0, DECAY 460 ms, SUSTAIN 0 %
- Listen for: the timbre bending.

steps.title: Harden
steps.why:
- CUTOFF 1.2 kHz
- Envelope 2 RELEASE 30 ms
- OVERDRIVE 50 %
- Listen for: a plastic, metallic bass.

sounds.name: UK Garage Bass
sounds.ref: In the style of Artful Dodger — “Re-Rewind”
sounds.blurb: A deep, round, sliding sub bass for a shuffling groove.
sounds.how: Garage bass is a round sine that slides between notes. A sine, a touch of saw for definition, and glide.

steps.title: Round
steps.why:
- OSC 1 SHAPE sine → saw
- OSC 1 level 100 %
- CUTOFF 304 Hz
- Listen for: a round bass.

steps.title: Slide
steps.why:
- GLIDE on, time 90 ms
- Envelope 2 DECAY 460 ms, SUSTAIN 70 %, RELEASE 48 ms
- Listen for: notes sliding.

sounds.name: Grime Square Bass
sounds.ref: In the style of Wiley — “Eskimo”
sounds.blurb: A cold, hollow, icy square-wave bass.
sounds.how: Grime’s “eski” sound is a bare square wave, short and cold. An open square, a short envelope, no effects.

steps.title: A bare square
steps.why:
- OSC 1 SHAPE square
- OSC 1 level 90 %
- CUTOFF 2.3 kHz
- Listen for: a cold, hollow tone.

steps.title: Short
steps.why:
- Envelope 2 DECAY 300 ms, SUSTAIN 30 %, RELEASE 30 ms
- Listen for: icy notes.

sounds.name: Reggae Organ Bubble
sounds.ref: In the style of Bob Marley and the Wailers
sounds.blurb: A bouncing, percussive organ “bubble” on the off-beats.
sounds.how: The reggae bubble is short organ chords on the off-beats. A gated organ with a click from Envelope 2 on the filter.

steps.title: Organ
steps.why:
- OSC 1 SHAPE sine
- OSC 2 SHAPE square, OCTAVE +1 oct
- OSC 1 level 50 %, OSC 2 20 %
- CUTOFF 600 Hz
- Listen for: an organ tone.

steps.title: Click
steps.why:
- ENV ROUTING Env 1 Aux / Env 2 Filter+Gate: the volume opens with the key; Envelope 2 runs the filter
- Envelope 2 AMOUNT +2.0, DECAY 75 ms, SUSTAIN 30 %
- Listen for: short, clicking chords.

steps.title: Room
steps.why:
- EFFECT on, TYPE Rotating speaker, TIME 30 %, DEPTH/MIX 60 %, FBACK/MISC 40 %
- REVERB on, MIX 20 %, DECAY 30 %
- Listen for: a bubbling organ.

context.env2.decay: How much click each chord has.

sounds.name: Dub Siren
sounds.ref: In the style of King Tubby
sounds.blurb: A wailing siren drowned in long, runaway echoes.
sounds.how: The dub siren is a rising tone into a tape echo turned up until it nearly runs away. LFO 1, a sawtooth on pitch, makes it whoop.

steps.title: Tone
steps.why:
- OSC 1 SHAPE square
- OSC 1 level 80 %
- CUTOFF 2.3 kHz
- Listen for: a hollow tone.

steps.title: Whoop
steps.why:
- LFO 1 DEST Osc All Freq, FREQUENCY 2.75 Hz, AMOUNT +3.5, SHAPE Sawtooth: rising, then dropping
- Listen for: a whooping siren.

steps.title: Runaway echo
steps.why:
- EFFECT on, TYPE Tape delay 2, TIME 60 %, DEPTH/MIX 50 %, FBACK/MISC 85 %: repeats that almost never die
- REVERB on, MIX 30 %, DECAY 50 %
- Listen for: a siren in a dub echo.

sounds.name: Warped Polysynth
sounds.ref: In the style of Tame Impala — “Let It Happen”
sounds.blurb: A woozy, out-of-tune, phasing chord, as if the synth were melting.
sounds.how: Turned up, VINTAGE lets each voice wander far from the others. With a phaser it sounds like a polysynth melting in the sun.

steps.title: Saws
steps.why:
- OSC 1 level 50 %, OSC 2 50 %
- OSC 2 PITCH +0.1 st
- CUTOFF 600 Hz
- Listen for: a buzz.

steps.title: Melt
steps.why:
- VINTAGE 90 %: each voice wanders a long way
- Listen for: a woozy, sour chord.

steps.title: Phase
steps.why:
- Envelope 2 ATTACK 30 ms, RELEASE 300 ms
- EFFECT on, TYPE Phaser, TIME 40 %, DEPTH/MIX 70 %, FBACK/MISC 60 %
- REVERB on, MIX 30 %, DECAY 50 %
- Listen for: a melting polysynth.

sounds.name: Shoegaze Wall
sounds.ref: In the style of My Bloody Valentine — “Only Shallow”
sounds.blurb: A wall of noisy, bending, blurred chords.
sounds.how: Shoegaze blurs chords into noise and bends them. White noise in the mixer, OVERDRIVE, a wobbly tape echo and LFO 1 bending the pitch slowly.

steps.title: Noise in the chord
steps.why:
- OSC 1 level 30 %, OSC 2 30 %, NOISE white 30 %
- OSC 2 PITCH +0.2 st
- CUTOFF 600 Hz
- Listen for: a noisy chord.

steps.title: Bend
steps.why:
- LFO 1 DEST Osc All Freq, FREQUENCY 0.56 Hz, AMOUNT +0.9: the chord bending slowly, like a whammy bar
- Listen for: bending chords.

steps.title: Wall
steps.why:
- OVERDRIVE 30 %
- EFFECT on, TYPE Tape delay 2, TIME 50 %, DEPTH/MIX 40 %, FBACK/MISC 50 %
- REVERB on, MIX 50 %, DECAY 70 %
- Listen for: a wall of blurred noise.

sounds.name: Motorik Pulse
sounds.ref: In the style of Neu! — “Hallogallo”
sounds.blurb: A steady, driving, hypnotic eighth-note pulse.
sounds.how: Motorik is a relentless steady pulse. A driven saw pluck in even eighths on one note, with a slow LFO moving the tone.

steps.title: Saw
steps.why:
- OSC 1 level 80 %, OSC 1 SUB 30 %
- CUTOFF 304 Hz, RESONANCE 30 %, DRIVE 60 %
- Listen for: a driven buzz.

steps.title: Pulse
steps.why:
- Envelope 1 AMOUNT +2.0, DECAY 190 ms, SUSTAIN 20 %
- Envelope 2 DECAY 300 ms, SUSTAIN 40 %, RELEASE 30 ms
- Listen for: a steady pulse.

steps.title: Drift
steps.why:
- LFO 2 DEST Cutoff, FREQUENCY 0.28 Hz, AMOUNT +1.5
- EFFECT on, TYPE Tape delay 1, TIME 40 %, DEPTH/MIX 20 %, FBACK/MISC 30 %
- Listen for: a hypnotic, driving pulse.

sounds.name: Punk Organ
sounds.ref: In the style of Suicide — “Ghost Rider”
sounds.blurb: A cheap, distorted organ riff smeared with echo.
sounds.how: Martin Rev played a battered organ through effects. A thin, gated organ, the Distortion effect, and a lot of reverb.

steps.title: Cheap organ
steps.why:
- OSC 1 SHAPE pulse 32 %
- OSC 1 level 70 %
- CUTOFF 1.2 kHz
- ENV ROUTING Env 1 Aux / Env 2 Filter+Gate: the volume opens with the key; Envelope 2 runs the filter
- Envelope 2 AMOUNT 0: the filter stays where CUTOFF puts it
- Listen for: a thin, cheap organ.

steps.title: Dirt
steps.why:
- EFFECT on, TYPE Distortion, TIME 50 %, DEPTH/MIX 60 %, FBACK/MISC 50 %
- Listen for: a fuzzy organ.

steps.title: Smear
steps.why:
- REVERB on, MIX 50 %, DECAY 70 %
- Listen for: a distorted, echoing riff.

sounds.name: Oscillator Chime
sounds.ref: In the style of Silver Apples — “Oscillations”
sounds.blurb: A pulsing, chiming pattern of pure oscillator tones.
sounds.how: Simeon played banks of oscillators by hand. Pure sines, the arpeggiator in Assign order, and a tape echo.

steps.title: Sines
steps.why:
- OSC 1 SHAPE sine
- OSC 2 SHAPE sine, OCTAVE +1 oct
- OSC 1 level 70 %, OSC 2 30 %
- CUTOFF 4.6 kHz
- Listen for: pure tones.

steps.title: In order played
steps.why:
Assign plays the notes in the order the keys went down.
- ARPEGGIATOR on, MODE Assign, OCTAVE 1 octave, CLK DIV 1/8, BPM 140 BPM
- Envelope 2 DECAY 300 ms, SUSTAIN 20 %, RELEASE 120 ms
- Listen for: a chiming pattern.

steps.title: Echo
steps.why:
- EFFECT on, TYPE Tape delay 1, TIME 50 %, DEPTH/MIX 30 %, FBACK/MISC 40 %
- Listen for: pulsing oscillator chimes.

context.arp.mode: Assign: the order the keys were pressed.

sounds.name: Dream-Pop Shimmer
sounds.ref: In the style of Cocteau Twins — “Heaven or Las Vegas”
sounds.blurb: A shimmering, liquid, chorused chord that glistens.
sounds.how: Dream pop is shimmer and space. A bright, gentle chord through a slow flanger, into a long, bright reverb with predelay.

steps.title: Bright
steps.why:
- OSC 1 SHAPE saw → square
- OSC 2 SHAPE sine → saw, OCTAVE +1 oct, PITCH +0.1 st
- OSC 1 level 60 %, OSC 2 40 %
- CUTOFF 1.2 kHz
- Listen for: a bright, gentle chord.

steps.title: Shimmer
steps.why:
- Envelope 2 ATTACK 75 ms, RELEASE 700 ms
- EFFECT on, TYPE Flanger, TIME 15 %, DEPTH/MIX 50 %, FBACK/MISC 50 %
- Listen for: a liquid shimmer.

steps.title: Space
steps.why:
- REVERB on, MIX 60 %, DECAY 80 %, PREDELAY 60 ms, TONE thinner 40 %
- Listen for: a glistening, dreamy chord.
